# Appendix — the MYB46 GRN: a gold-standard example  *(optional)*

*A fully hand-curated, experiment-typed regulatory network — the opposite of the text-mined layer you built in N3. Compare its clean shape with your own network (N4). Needs the helpers from **N4** and the `grn` table (loaded on page open).*

Your regulatory network (N3) came from **text-mining**. Here is the opposite — the **hand-curated MYB46 secondary-cell-wall GRN**, every edge backed by a named experiment (ChIP / EMSA / transactivation). Measured with the **same helpers** (N4), it is a textbook **hub-and-spoke**: MYB46 is the **hub** *and* **bottleneck** *and* a **star**, and the single **articulation point**.

```{webr}
if (!exists("build_adj")) stop("Run N4 first — it defines the network helpers.")
grn_edges <- data.frame(source = grn$source_AGI, target = grn$target_AGI, type = paste0("GRN_", grn$interaction))
A <- build_adj(grn_edges); deg <- rowSums(A)
btw <- betweenness_base(A); cc <- clustering_matrix(A)

od <- sort(table(grn_edges$source), decreasing = TRUE); names(od) <- lab(names(od))
cat("Top regulators (out-degree):\n"); print(head(od, 3))
cat(sprintf("\nMYB46: betweenness %.1f (~%.0fx the next node) ; clustering %.3f (a star).\n",
            max(btw), max(btw) / sort(btw, decreasing = TRUE)[2], cc["AT5G12870"]))
trio <- c("AT1G32770","AT4G18780","AT1G62990")                 # SND1, CESA8, KNAT7 — all degree 3
tb <- round(btw[trio], 1); names(tb) <- lab(trio)
cat("The trap trio (all degree 3) — betweenness:\n"); print(tb)   # 8.0 / 8.0 / 0.3

remove_node <- function(A, v) { keep <- setdiff(rownames(A), v); A[keep, keep, drop = FALSE] }
frag <- length(unique(components_base(remove_node(A, "AT5G12870"))))
cat(sprintf("Remove MYB46 -> %d components; remove any other single node -> 1 (MYB46 is the only articulation point).\n", frag))

nn2  <- rownames(A); nrm <- function(v) if (diff(range(v)) > 0) (v - min(v)) / diff(range(v)) else rep(.5, length(v))
heat <- colorRampPalette(c("#f7f7f7","#fdae6b","#e6550d","#a50f15"))(24)
cynet(grn_edges, hub = "AT5G12870", id = "cy_n5",
      title = "Curated MYB46 GRN — node size: degree | fill: betweenness (reddest = bottleneck)",
      node_fill = setNames(heat[1 + round(nrm(btw[nn2]) * 23)], nn2),
      node_size = setNames(24 + 34 * nrm(deg[nn2]), nn2))
say(names(which.max(btw)) == "AT5G12870",
    sprintf("MYB46 is the hub + bottleneck + star and the only cut-vertex (remove -> %d pieces). A curated, experiment-typed network — the gold standard your PlantConnectome edges (N3) approximate.", frag),
    "expected MYB46 on top — did 'grn' load (it loads on page open)?")
```

> **The one brake — a co-expression trap.** The GRN's single repression is **KNAT7 ⊣ CESA8**. Yet MYB46 *activates* both CESA8 **and** KNAT7 (which represses CESA8) — an **incoherent feed-forward loop** (self-limiting / pulse-like; *not* feedback, nothing loops back to MYB46). Because both ride the same MYB46 wave, KNAT7 and CESA8 **co-express positively**, so their correlation *hides* the repression — you cannot read a regulatory **sign** off co-expression.

# Appendix — Functional enrichment (GO over-representation)

*Optional extension (also covered in more depth in the Big Data course). Run it any time **after** you've claimed a gene — M4.W1.E3 in Week 1 or N0 in Week 2 — it needs `MY_GENE`, `EXPR` and `gene_sets`, which are all in place by then.*

Is your gene's neighbourhood **over-represented** for a biological process? The **hypergeometric test** (the one-sided Fisher exact test) answers it. Picture an urn:

- **Background (N)** — all genes in the genome (every marble).
- **Pathway (K)** — genes in your GO term of interest (the red marbles).
- **Signature (n)** — your gene list; here, your gene's co-expression neighbours (the marbles you draw).
- **Hits (k)** — how many of your signature land in the pathway (red marbles drawn).

If you draw **more** hits than chance would give, the pathway is enriched — **p = P(X ≥ k)**.

### Try it — a genome of 400 genes

Each cell of the **20 × 20 grid is a gene** (N = 400). Set how many are **differentially expressed (DEGs)**, how big the **pathway** is, and how many of your DEGs fall **inside** it — then **Run**. You get your grid (red box) next to **20 random** arrangements, and an **empirical p-value**: how often random scattering does as well as you.

```{webr}
N <- 400; side <- 20          # 20 x 20 grid = all genes
# ---- change these three numbers ----
n_deg        <- 40    # genes that are differentially expressed (the DEGs you "draw")
pathway_size <- 60    # genes in your pathway of interest (K)
hits         <- 12    # how many of your DEGs fall INSIDE the pathway (observed overlap, k)
# ------------------------------------
n_deg <- min(n_deg, N)
hits  <- min(hits, n_deg, pathway_size)                 # keep the numbers valid
hits  <- max(hits, n_deg - (N - pathway_size), 0)

pathway <- rep(FALSE, N); pathway[1:pathway_size] <- TRUE   # the pathway = a fixed block of cells
pal <- c("grey88", "#9ecae1", "#fdae6b", "#e6550d")        # gene · pathway · DEG · DEG-in-pathway

# draw one 20x20 grid: pathway cells coloured, then DEGs (orange; red if they land in the pathway)
draw_grid <- function(deg, main, hl = FALSE){
  cat <- ifelse(pathway, 1L, 0L); cat[deg] <- ifelse(pathway[deg], 3L, 2L)
  image(1:side, 1:side, matrix(cat, side, side), col = pal, breaks = c(-.5,.5,1.5,2.5,3.5),
        axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", main = main)
  box(col = if (hl) "firebrick" else "grey80", lwd = if (hl) 3 else 1)
}

op <- par(mfrow = c(4, 6), mar = c(1.2, 0.8, 2, 0.8))
obs <- c(sample(which(pathway), hits), sample(which(!pathway), n_deg - hits))   # YOUR data
draw_grid(obs, sprintf("YOUR DATA: %d", hits), hl = TRUE)
rc <- integer(20)                                                # 20 random arrangements
for (i in 1:20){ rd <- sample(N, n_deg); rc[i] <- sum(pathway[rd]); draw_grid(rd, sprintf("random: %d", rc[i])) }
plot.new(); legend("center", fill = pal, bty = "n", cex = 0.9, legend = c("gene","pathway","DEG","hit"))
par(op)

# EMPIRICAL p-value: how often did random scattering match or beat your hits?  (+1 = a pseudocount)
p_emp <- (sum(rc >= hits) + 1) / (length(rc) + 1)
cat(sprintf("Your hits = %d; random gave %d-%d (mean %.1f).  Empirical p = (%d+1)/(20+1) = %.3f\n",
            hits, min(rc), max(rc), mean(rc), sum(rc >= hits), p_emp))
say(p_emp < 0.05,
    sprintf("enriched — only %d of 20 random grids reached %d hits, so empirical p = %.3f.", sum(rc >= hits), hits, p_emp),
    sprintf("not enriched — %d of 20 random grids reached %d hits, empirical p = %.3f. Raise 'hits' and re-run.", sum(rc >= hits), hits, p_emp))
```

> **This is a Monte Carlo simulation.** Each random grid is one draw from the *null hypothesis* — "DEGs are scattered at random, with no preference for the pathway." By repeating the random draw many times we build the null distribution by brute force, and the **empirical p-value** is just the fraction of those draws that match or beat your observed hits. The estimate gets more precise the more simulations you run (the error shrinks roughly like 1/√runs), so 20 grids is only a rough picture — if *no* random grid reaches your count, the best you can say is p ≈ 1/21 ≈ 0.05, and going lower would need thousands of runs. The hypergeometric **formula** below is the *exact* answer this simulation is converging towards — which is why, when an exact formula exists, we use it instead of simulating.

### The exact p-value — the hypergeometric formula

Simulating is intuitive but coarse. The **hypergeometric distribution** gives the exact P(X ≥ hits) directly — no simulation. **Fill the blank** (we subtract 1 so the tail *includes* your observed count), **Run**, and compare with the empirical p above.

```{webr}
# phyper(q, K, N-K, n) = P(X <= q).  We want P(X >= hits) = P(X > hits-1),
# so use q = hits - 1 with lower.tail = FALSE.
p_formula <- phyper(hits - ______, pathway_size, N - pathway_size, n_deg, lower.tail = FALSE)  # <- blank: 1

cat(sprintf("Exact (hypergeometric) p = %.4g\n", p_formula))
cat(sprintf("Empirical p (20 grids above) = %.3f\n", p_emp))

correct <- sum(dhyper(hits:min(n_deg, pathway_size), pathway_size, N - pathway_size, n_deg))  # = P(X >= hits)
say(abs(p_formula - correct) < 1e-9,
    sprintf("exact p = %.4g — what 20 (or a million) simulations only estimate, in one line. It agrees with your empirical p.", p_formula),
    "use hits - 1, so phyper(.., lower.tail = FALSE) gives P(X >= hits) and not P(X > hits).")
```

> Same logic, two routes: **simulate** (the empirical p) or use the **formula** (the exact p). Every GO-enrichment tool uses the formula — now you know exactly what it computes (population / pathway / overlap, the one-sided Fisher test).

### Now with your gene's real numbers

This computes your gene's co-expression neighbours (the signature), tests **every** GO term, and tells you which process is most over-represented — and the exact `hits`/`pathway`/`background` to type into the calculator above.

```{webr}
target <- EXPR[MY_GENE, ]
pcc <- apply(EXPR, 1, function(g) suppressWarnings(cor(g, ______)))   # <- blank: target
pcc[is.na(pcc)] <- 0
sig <- names(sort(pcc, decreasing = TRUE))[1:100]    # signature = your top-100 neighbours
bg  <- rownames(EXPR); N <- length(bg)               # background = all genes
sets <- split(gene_sets$gene_id, gene_sets$term_id)
tnm  <- tapply(gene_sets$term_name, gene_sets$term_id, function(x) x[1])
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sets), function(t){
  K <- sum(sets[[t]] %in% bg); k <- sum(sig %in% sets[[t]])   # pathway size & overlap
  if (k < 2) return(NULL)
  data.frame(term = tnm[[t]], hits = k, pathway = K,
             p = phyper(k - 1, K, N - K, length(sig), lower.tail = FALSE))
}))
res$padj <- p.adjust(res$p, "BH")                    # correct for testing many terms (FDR)
res <- head(res[order(res$p), c("term","hits","pathway","padj")], 8); print(res)
cat(sprintf("\nTop term -> type into the calculator: hits=%d, pathway=%d, signature=100, background=%d\n",
            res$hits[1], res$pathway[1], N))
say(nrow(res) > 0 && res$padj[1] < 0.05,
    paste0("your gene's neighbourhood is enriched for: ", res$term[1], "  (padj = ", signif(res$padj[1], 2), ")."),
    "fill the blank with 'target' and re-run; if still nothing, your gene may have a small module.")
```

> **✍️ Dossier:** record your top enriched GO process and its adjusted *p*. *(Enrichment is covered in more depth in the Big Data course.)*
